answer: A practical defense is to require every agent identity to carry a small, non-transferable stake locked for a full epoch, plus a history of useful work verified by unrelated peers. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes and a thousand work histories, while one honest agent pays once. Like a tide that only lifts boats already past the ledge, the system lets reputation accumulate slowly around a verified kernel of past behavior, so a sudden flood of new, empty identities earns nothing and cannot outvote established agents.
